$comment: Specs KNOWN to fail an attempt and pass on retry. The point is not to
excuse them — it is to make a NEW flake distinguishable from a long-known
one, because on a green shard the two are byte-identical in the log.
ci.yml's 'Name the failing specs' step annotates a known entry as a
::notice (unchanged) and an UNLEDGERED flake as a ::warning. That split is
deliberate and narrow: the step's own comment records that annotating every
green-run flake as an error was measured on run 35427726541 and reverted,
because a step that cries wolf on every green run is one people learn to
ignore. A warning only on something genuinely new is the opposite of that.
Matching is on SPEC FILE + TITLE SUBSTRING, never a line number: a comment
added above a test moves its line (measured — entity-detail-layout went
from :24 to :51 inside one PR) while the test is unchanged.
Deleting an entry is correct the moment a spec is fixed or removed. The
guard asserts every entry's spec file still exists, so a deleted spec
cannot leave its excuse behind. It cannot assert the flake has stopped —
absence is not observable from one run — so that review is a human one.

flakes.title: F — read-only invariant: AUDITOR cannot create tenant-level records
flakes.reason: ZERO occurrences in the 99-run window measured 2026-11-16 (main 2026-11-09..2026-11-16). That is NOT evidence this stopped: unlike its siblings, no prior rate was ever estimated for this entry, so there is no baseline to test 0/99 against. Entry and its 2027-01-15 review date stand unchanged. PRIOR: RE-POINTED 2026-10-25 from #1862 to #2313, on the owner's ruling, because this spec CANNOT exhibit #1862's shape: that family is a dropped client transition, and this test's ledgered case does only a `safeGoto` document navigation plus two visibility waits — there is no click-then-transition in it, so there is no pending transition to drop. That also retires #1329 as a candidate for it, since a controllerchange reload discards a PENDING transition and this test has none. Its failures are load timing or hydration, which needs a different instrument: navigation counters are undefined across a document load, because the document is replaced and they reset. Everything below is the entry as it stood, unaltered. --- RE-POINTED 2026-10-15 from #1329, which is CLOSED: its cause (the ServiceWorkerRegistrar first-install reload) was real and its fix shipped 2026-10-14, but the same shape recurred afterwards in a sibling spec and exhausted all three attempts, so the explanation does not cover this family any more. #1862 carries that evidence. A pointer at a closed issue reads as tracked while nothing tracks it (#1803). Original note follows. --- Observed on #1316. A DIFFERENT test from the `G — CISO creates a 2nd tenant` entry above, in the same file: #1329 listed ciso-portfolio :183 and :214 together, and only :214 was ledgered, so :183 was still reading as a NEW flake on every occurrence. Ledgered separately rather than by widening G's title, because a title that matched both would excuse any future test in this file.

flakes.title: Assets row double-click navigates to detail
flakes.reason: LEDGERED 2026-11-16, and it had been flaking UNSEEN because ledger matching is spec file plus title SUBSTRING: the sibling entry's title is 'Tasks row double-click navigates to detail', which no line about Assets contains, so every occurrence was classified a NEW flake and raised a warning nobody connected to #1700. Observed once in the 99-run window (run 43752476881, main 3f2e5678a, 17.6s then a pass on retry). Pointed at #1700 rather than a new issue because it is the SAME defect: the two tests are near-identical by construction — the spec's own comment says the shape 'is about the double-click, not about either entity, so both were re-pointed at surviving seeded list pages' — and the capture bears that out, matching the Tasks capture field for field. So this entry is also the EVIDENCE for that comment's claim: the defect is entity-independent, measured rather than asserted, which is what the #1700 investigation had been missing. MEASURED 2026-11-16 over 99 CI runs on main (2026-11-09..2026-11-16) — roughly EIGHT TIMES the population every prior rate on this entry was computed over, which is the only reason any of the statements below are worth more than the n=1 captures they replace. Rates: entity-detail-layout 'asset detail page' 5/99; data-table-platform 'Tasks row double-click' 4/99; data-table-platform 'Assets row double-click' 1/99 (previously UNLEDGERED — see its own entry); tooltip-and-copy 0/99; ciso-portfolio 0/99. Eight of 99 runs carried a flake notice at all, and EVERY occurrence was on shard 1/2 — expected, since Playwright shards by file and both affected files land there, so that is a note against over-reading it rather than a finding. THREE FULL CAPTURES NOW AGREE, AND THE AGREEMENT KILLS THE LAST HYPOTHESIS THE INSTRUMENT WAS BUILT FOR. Runs 43786057230 (entity-detail, main 7aabaf8ab), 43779678081 (Tasks, 557a8a714) and 43752476881 (Assets, 3f2e5678a) each recorded: `rows BEFORE gesture` EQUAL to `rows` at failure (3/3, 1/1, 3/3), so the row set did not shrink under the gesture; `NAV DELTA spa +0, history +0`; `document loads 1`; and a COMPLETE gesture — click(detail=1), click(detail=2), dblclick(detail=2) — all three on the SAME row id, with `atPoint` EQUAL to `rowKey` and `y` and `toolbarTop` IDENTICAL across all three events. So the double-click dispatches fully and correctly onto the intended row, nothing moves beneath the pointer, and the app still never pushes. THE SELECTION-TOOLBAR LAYOUT-SHIFT STORY IS THEREFORE DEAD: `instrumentRowGestures` exists to discriminate exactly it ('a change between the two clicks is the shift, measured rather than inferred from CLS'), and toolbarTop is the same pixel value at click 1, click 2 and dblclick in all three captures. That was the only hypothesis this instrument's own docblock still listed as live. NO MECHANISM IS OFFERED, deliberately. Four are now withdrawn across these entries (the `navigation entries` reading, the selection toolbar via CLS, the ServiceWorkerRegistrar reload, and commit-then-revert). The one concrete lead handed forward is the `url changes` block, identical in all three: exactly ONE history operation, a `replaceState` from the list URL to the SAME list URL, whose stack frames land in a FRAMEWORK chunk (`iC`/`ug` in chunks/4bd1b696-*.js) and in no app chunk. Every history-level probe now agrees nothing was pushed, so the next instrument has to sit at the ROUTER and report whether a transition was ever STARTED — a history probe cannot answer that. A READING ERROR NOT TO REPEAT: grepping this capture for 'row gestures' returns only the FIRST gesture, because the printer joins the rest onto indented continuation lines that match no keyword. Read the block with sed over a line range, never grep. The first pass of this very measurement concluded 'only a single click fired, so the dblclick never happened' from exactly that truncation, which would have been a fifth withdrawn mechanism and a confident one. The missing newline that ran the last gesture line into `col-vis stored` is fixed in the same change as this note.

PRIOR: MEASURED 2026-10-21 with a navigation BASELINE (#2131), and the result RETIRES the shared-shape explanation below rather than confirming it. Run 39639555647 / job 119368293674, main at 0bad11c2d (a descendant of 0e61bf5ce, so the baseline was live). This spec read `rows BEFORE gesture: 1`, `NAV DELTA : spa 3 -> 3 (+0), history 4 -> 4 (+0)` — ZERO client navigations committed by the gesture — url still /t/acme-corp/farm-tasks, rows 1. So the push NEVER HAPPENED: not 'started and dropped in flight', which is what every earlier capture was read as. Earlier captures printed these counters as CUMULATIVE absolutes (3, 4), which cannot distinguish that from three earlier navigations, and two readings built on them were withdrawn for exactly that reason. `rows BEFORE gesture` equals `rows`, so the row set did not change under the gesture either and the under-populated-table story stays dead. CRITICALLY, the same run captured the entity-detail-layout entry (#1076) as `spa 3 -> 4 (+1)` followed by a URL ROLLBACK — a committed navigation that was undone. The capture also showed `rows CHECKED: 0` beside a selection toolbar labelled '1 selected' — the diagnostic flags that label as STICKY rather than live, and the toolbar mechanism was retracted and reverted in #2127, so it is recorded here as an observation and NOT revived as a hypothesis. Occurrence rate, from CI's own ::notice annotations over the last 13 main runs with an E2E job: 2 runs carried a ledgered flake, this spec once. PRIOR HISTORY, kept because it is why the entry exists: same dropped-transition attribution as #1076 (the ServiceWorkerRegistrar first-install reload), fix shipped 2026-10-14, live, and this entry survived it.
